content.introduction: The Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) typically meets eight times a year, with the possibility of additional meetings if necessary. Each meeting includes discussions on monetary policy options to achieve maximum employment and price stability. The FOMC Secretariat, led by Chair Powell, prepares an agenda that includes reports on open market operations, the economic situation, and monetary policy alternatives, as well as any special items. The meeting usually concludes with a formal vote on policy actions around 12:00 p.m. (ET), followed by the release of the statement at 2:00 p.m. (ET) and a press conference by Chair Powell at 2:30 p.m. (ET).
body:
First off, Chair Powell works with the FOMC Secretariat, currently Joshua Gallin, to produce an agenda for the Committee meeting. It includes standard topics such as reports on open market operations, the economic situation, and monetary policy alternatives, as well as any special items. Special items for the May meeting could plausibly include an update on developments in the banking sector as well as a report on the effects of a potential U.S. default. The Secretariat then sends the finished [...] Ahead of each meeting, the Secretariat also distributes memos to the FOMC participants. These memos generally cover the economic, financial, and monetary issues as described by the Fed Board staff. [...] At last, the meeting normally ends around 12:00 p.m. (ET) with each FOMC member formally voting to approve the policy action and statement.

The statement gets released to the public at 2:00 p.m. (ET) and Fed Chair Powell then gives a press conference at 2:30 p.m. (ET) and the market fun ensues.

## More articles by Jonathan Schwarz

The FOMC holds eight regularly scheduled meetings during the year and other meetings as needed. Links to policy statements and minutes are in the calendars below. The minutes of regularly scheduled meetings are released three weeks after the date of the policy decision. Committee membership changes at the first regularly scheduled meeting of the year.

Armed with this wealth of up-to-date national, international, and regional information, the FOMC discusses the monetary policy options that would best move the economy toward the Fed’s dual mandate objectives given by Congress: maximum employment and price stability. The FOMC meeting concludes with a decision on the stance of policy.

## How It Works: The FOMC Voting Rotation Among Reserve Banks [...] The Federal Open Market Committee typically meets 8 times a year in the Board Room at the Eccles Building in Washington, D.C. When necessary, members will meet by a teleconference. If economic conditions require additional meetings, the FOMC can and does meet more often.

At each regularly scheduled 2-day FOMC meeting: [...] Federal Open Market Committee

   Gathering Data

   Safety and Soundness

   Discount Window Lending 
   Term Auction Facility 
   Financial Services 
   Providing Financial Services
